election._note: By law no later than 25 March 2029; Wikipedia 'Next German federal election'. MMP reduced to national PR — see docs/electoral-systems.md.

dissolution._note: Art. 68 GG: the Bundestag can be dissolved only after the Chancellor calls a confidence vote and loses it, and only within 21 days of that loss. No confidence-vote command exists at V1.1c, so this refuses the player's command outright rather than half-model it. Elections must follow within 60 days (Art. 39). bundeswahlleiterin.de, 'Early elections'; ukconstitutionallaw.org, 'An Aversion to Weimar'.

head_of_state._note: The Bundespräsident, elected by the Federal Convention for a five-year term; last elected February 2022, so the next is due February 2027. Ceremonial -- no reader beyond the government panel. Wikipedia, 'President of Germany'.
head_of_state.title: Federal President

amendment._note: Art. 79(2) GG: a Basic Law amendment requires a 2/3 majority of BOTH the Bundestag's statutory membership and the Bundesrat's votes. Only the Bundestag half is modelled -- there is no Bundesrat in this game -- so this is the harder of the two real hurdles, not the easier. See docs/amendment-model.md's reachability sweep: measurably unreachable for Germany's authored six-party roster even at full term-start cohesion, and left at the real figure rather than detuned. Bundestag.de, 'Amending the Basic Law'.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Art. 79(3) GG, the eternity clause: no amendment may touch the federal structure or the Art. 1/20 principles it entrenches, which as a practical matter puts the form of state beyond amendment at all.

formation._note: Chancellor elected by the Bundestag with an absolute majority of the statutory membership (Kanzlermehrheit); removable only by a constructive vote of no confidence that simultaneously elects a successor. Art. 63 and 67 GG; bundestag.de 'Election of the Federal Chancellor'.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. V1.2a starting policy, derived from France's anchor (see FRA.json): VAT 19% is Germany's own statutory standard rate (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024'). Income and corporate are France's 20/25 scaled by Germany's OECD Revenue Statistics personal/corporate tax-to-GDP share against France's -- income tax leans similar, corporate revenue (Gewerbesteuer included) runs higher, hence 21/29.9. Spending is France's split scaled by general government expenditure of 49.4% of GDP against France's 57.3% (TheGlobalEconomy.com / OECD Government at a Glance 2025).
